A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton

recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Bio: Gabriel, known on air as Slick Dissident, co-hosts InnerVerse's Vibe Rant show and is a longtime recurring guest on the podcast. He teaches occult symbolism and tarot on his YouTube channel, ranging across the Major Arcana, the esoteric Enneagram, mythology and archetype, mystic linguistics, and the symbolism hidden in popular film. He is best known for Tarot-tories, his own system mapping the 22 Major Arcana and zodiac archetypes onto the geography of the United States.
recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Name: Gabe (Slick Dissident)
recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Role: Co-host of Vibe Rant; teacher of occult symbolism & tarot

recZOKCUcQhghoKqF.Bio: Kayleigh Berkana is an astrologer who has appeared as a recurring panelist on InnerVerse group discussions (alongside Slick Dissident, Mario Garza, and others) covering topics like Lovecraftian mythology, Jack Parsons, and occult symbolism.
recZOKCUcQhghoKqF.Name: Kayleigh Berkana

reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Bio: Mario Garza is the artist and researcher behind Symbolic Studies, a project sharing symbolic insights on the zodiac, mythology, folklore and world religions, with astrology as its foundation. A lifelong artist who has worked as an art director and graphic designer for nearly 25 years, he runs Symbolic Studies from the Pacific Northwest alongside his wife Michelle, who co-hosts the podcast with him. His work traces syncretic threads across tarot, occultism and comparative religion, including the argument that the major deities of antiquity were originally polar gods before a solar model was laid over them. He also offers symbolic birth chart and tarot readings, private lessons and freelance design.
reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Name: Mario Garza

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Juan Ayala's Portrait of Lovecraft", "body": "Juan Ayala sets the stage by calling Lovecraft one of history's most prolific letter writers, with estimates he puts at 75,000 to 100,000 letters, many as long as books, written by a man Juan describes as a virtual hermit who never really held a job. Juan traces the mythos to a childhood obsession with the Arabian Nights, which he says inspired the alter ego Abdul Alhazred, supposed author of the Necronomicon, and to a grandfather's library said to hold the Picatrix. He names Lovecraft's racism plainly while crediting his reach into films like The Thing and Color Out of Space, plus video, card and board games."}, {"title": "Pluto as Lovecraft's Planet", "body": "Kayleigh Berkana comes at Lovecraft through Pluto, a planet she says astrologers tie to darkness before deep transformation and rebirth. She recounts Percival Lowell's search for a Planet X beyond Neptune and Clyde Tombaugh's discovery on February 18, 1930, noting that Lovecraft, a keen student of astronomy who wrote for journals, lived until 1937, and she places the discovery in Cancer near Ursa Major and Ursa Minor. Gabe says the first recorded hint of Pluto fell on Lovecraft's nineteenth birthday, the panel notes a feature on Pluto named for Cthulhu, and Gabe frames the coming American Pluto return to its 1776 position as the scale of the spell."}, {"title": "How Occultists Adopted the Mythos", "body": "Mario Garza argues that however Lovecraft's work came to be, he was tapped in, updating an older pantheon for modern sensibilities, and that his influence runs through an underground of black magical books and groups. Mario says he found a reverence for the north, the North Star and Ursa Major that goes largely unnoticed, and that some Lovecraftian groups vet initiates by whether their psyche survives a ritual, while others treat the North Star as an astral gateway out and back. Pointing to the steady stream of rituals, spells and new versions of the Necronomicon, he says he doubts people would keep doing this if it did not work."}, {"title": "Fiction, Fear and the Dreaming God", "body": "Gabe floats the theory that the whole Lovecraft web may be the largest black magic LARP of all time, run by masters of fiction, while Chance questions the idea of entities outside reality and frames Mark Passio's notion of cosmic abandonment as a perspective gap that nature's symbolic correspondences can close. The panel turns to Azathoth, the blind idiot god whose dream is said to be our reality, and the conversation reads this as fictionalized pop gnosticism, suggesting that people who crack open expanded consciousness while carrying fear and impurity find that fear amplified back at them."}, {"title": "Taking Back the Power From Fear", "body": "The closing strand turns from horror to agency. Gabe says horror fans tend to adopt a passive posture while he steers his imagination, and he reads the image of Andrew Jackson slaying the many headed bank monster as a way of stirring inherited fears of financial collapse. Kayleigh counters that anyone can read a chart but no chart shows the human soul or its willpower, and Chance closes by arguing that believing in any boogeyman greater than our divine spark only breeds bigger ones, insisting we are the imagination that dreams reality. In a last exchange, the panel weighs Lovecraft's line that fear is the strongest emotion against love."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Get ready to release the Kraken tonight as we crack into the deranged skull of H.P. Lovecraft and decode his C'Thonic mythology, it's cultural influence, astrological significance, and symbolic strangeness. This super-panel live stream starring Slick Dissident (Gabriel), Juan from The Juan on Juan Podcast, Mario Garza from Symbolic Studies, and astrologer Kayleigh Berkana, might just leave you feeling the aybss staring back.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Ursa Major as the northern gateway", "body": "Mario Garza builds the members' hour around the North. Drawing on Simon's The Gates of the Necronomicon, which he credits to Peter Levenda, along with Levenda's The Dark Lord and Stairway to Heaven, Mario argues that many older traditions treated Ursa Major, Ursa Minor and the pole star as a sky clock and an exit from this world. He links the Egyptian thigh of the bull, the adze used in the opening of the mouth rite, and the number seven to the Big Dipper, while noting that seven stars are sometimes, not always, a reference to the great bear."}, {"title": "Nine, seven and the cube as symbolic numbers", "body": "Juan Ayala opens the second hour with the Pythagorean view of nine as the number of humanity, one short of the sacred ten, and later turns to seven, the heptad, which he says stood for law. He connects the Kabbalistic Sabbath to a central point radiating six directions, the faces of a cube. Slick Dissident adds his own decode of the Platonic solids inside the cube and the magic square of the moon, while Kayleigh Berkana ties seven to Libra and Saturn. Each speaker presents these links as interpretation and symbolic play rather than settled fact."}, {"title": "Reading Lovecraft through his birth chart", "body": "Kayleigh Berkana walks the panel through H.P. Lovecraft's natal chart, starting with Libra rising and Venus, the chart ruler, in the twelfth house, which she reads as a private, behind the scenes temperament. She points to the Moon conjunct Uranus in the first house as a source of restless discomfort, Jupiter in the fourth house for his late return home, and a grand air trine as the signature of a gifted writer. Juan Ayala supplies biography, including his grandfather's reported business losses, which Kayleigh compares with Pluto and Neptune in the eighth house."}, {"title": "Ritual, belief and protecting yourself", "body": "Juan Ayala asks Mario Garza how to study dark material without being pulled into someone else's ritual, and shares secondhand stories of translators troubled by strange activity. Mario answers that intention and approach matter most, and that he treats even a notorious deck like the Sola Busca tarot as a study tool. Kayleigh Berkana describes clearing her space before and after opening charts. Chance Garton frames all ritual as intent and consent, arguing that belief can be met with belief, and Mario and Kayleigh close on self knowledge and free will over fear."}, {"title": "Slick Dissident's New Orleans spell thesis", "body": "Slick Dissident presents his most ambitious decode of the night, linking a reported Aleister Crowley ritual in New Orleans in 1907 to the Cthulhu story Lovecraft later set there, and placing the Cthulhu devil card over Louisiana on his tarotories map. He reads Hurricane Katrina, the broken levees, Providence's silverware trade and Peter Levenda's surname as layers of one deliberate working. He offers this openly as his own interpretation, saying it is either coincidence, magic or an enormous spell, and the panel treats it as a provocative theory to examine rather than a proven account."}]

I'm steering this ship, and I'm not letting anybody try to put me in a state of fear.", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "There's this reverence and this nod to the north and the North Star and Ursa Major that I think goes really, really under the radar.", "author": "Mario Garza", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/94a2fe35-cc60-4591-8931-7e2b7af18c82/MARIO-GARZA.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "If we ever believe that such a boogeyman exists, there will always be a bigger one than that one, and then a bigger one than that one.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Anybody can look at a chart, but the one thing that you'll never see in the chart is the human soul, their individual willpower and their soul.", "author": "Kayleigh Berkana", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/5c923247-58f8-42f0-a64e-59357e5336f4/KAYLEIGH-BERKANA.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I like to keep it anagrams because anagrams are objective truth. You don't leave any letters out, you use all the letters, and it says something crystal clear.", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "We are the source, we are the imagination, we are God, the God that dreams reality into existence, all of us.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}]
